response.sql: SELECT SEX, AVG(patient_avg_PT) as avg_PT, AVG(patient_avg_ratio) as avg_ALP_GPT_ratio FROM (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.PT) as patient_avg_PT, AVG(CASE WHEN l.ALP IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT != 0 THEN l.ALP / l.GPT ELSE NULL END) as patient_avg_ratio FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`U-PRO` IS NULL OR l.`U-PRO` != '-' GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX) subquery GROUP BY SEX

assumptions.assumption: Lab records where U-PRO is NULL are included in the analysis, treating NULL as distinct from the '-' result. The request specifically states 'without a urine protein result of \'-\'', which the primary query interprets as excluding only '-' values, not missing values. Alternatively, all missing/invalid U-PRO values (NULL and '-') might need exclusion.

alternatives.interpretation: The phrase 'patients without a urine protein result of \'-\'' could filter at the patient level rather than the record level—include all lab records for patients who have no lab records with U-PRO = '-', rather than filtering individual records where U-PRO ≠ '-'. This would exclude entire patients if any of their lab records show U-PRO = '-'.
